home.subtitle: Discover sparse, interpretable predictive models from omics data.
home.description: Powered by gpredomics — a high-performance Rust engine for Binary, Ternary, and Ratio model languages using genetic algorithms, beam search, and Bayesian MCMC.

workflow.uploadDesc: Import your omics matrices (TSV/CSV) — training and optional test sets

workflow.analyzeDesc: Launch evolutionary search with real-time progress tracking

home.uploadDataDesc: Import your omics/metagenomics matrices (TSV/CSV) with flexible row or column orientation.
home.configureRunDesc: Choose algorithms (GA, Beam, MCMC), languages (binary, ternary, ratio), and tune parameters.
home.exploreResultsDesc: Browse model populations, inspect feature importance, and compare across runs.

algo.label: Algorithm
algo.desc: Search or learning method. The first seven (GA, Beam, MCMC, ACO, SA, LASSO, ILS) are gpredomics methods that produce small interpretable models; the others (Random Forest, SVM, Logistic Regression, XGBoost, LightGBM, Extra Trees, AdaBoost, KNN) are standard machine-learning baselines for comparison.

fit.label: Fit function
fit.desc: Objective metric for model evaluation. AUC is recommended for balanced classification.

language.label: Language
language.desc: Model languages to explore. Initial population is split among selected languages.

data_type.label: Data type
data_type.desc: Data transformations to apply. Multiple selections create separate model populations. Raw uses feature values directly. Prevalence binarizes features at threshold epsilon (presence/absence). Log applies natural log after epsilon flooring. Z-score standardizes each feature to mean=0, std=1 using training statistics (propagated to test to avoid data leakage).

seed.label: Random seed
seed.desc: Seed for reproducibility. Used in parent selection, crossover and mutation.

thread_number.label: Threads
thread_number.desc: Number of CPU threads for feature selection and fit computation.

cv.label: Cross-validation
cv.desc: Enable k-fold cross-validation. The dataset is split into outer folds; the algorithm trains on k-1 folds and validates on the held-out fold. This is a primary defense against overfitting and provides honest performance estimates. Combine with overfit_penalty for inner-fold regularization.

gpu.label: GPU acceleration
gpu.desc: Use GPU for fitness computation (GA and Beam only). Uses f32 precision.

epsilon.label: Epsilon
epsilon.desc: Threshold for prevalence data type, or replacement value below threshold for log data type.

k_penalty.label: k penalty
k_penalty.desc: Penalty multiplied by k (number of variables). Encourages parsimonious models.

fr_penalty.label: FR penalty
fr_penalty.desc: Used when fit is specificity or sensitivity. Subtracts (1 - symmetrical_metric) * fr_penalty.

bias_penalty.label: Bias penalty
bias_penalty.desc: Penalizes model fit when specificity or sensitivity falls below 0.5.

threshold_ci_n_bootstrap.label: Bootstrap samples (CI)
threshold_ci_n_bootstrap.desc: Number of bootstrap resamples for threshold confidence interval estimation. Since microbiome features are compositional (relative abundances), thresholds can be fragile and may not generalize across cohorts. Bootstrap CI quantifies this uncertainty by computing lower/upper bounds; samples falling in the uncertainty zone are rejected. Recommended: 200-1000. 0 = disabled.

threshold_ci_penalty.label: CI penalty
threshold_ci_penalty.desc: During evolution, models with wide threshold CI (many rejected samples) are penalized: fitness -= rejection_rate × penalty. This steers evolution toward models with stable, generalizable thresholds. Higher values (e.g. 0.8) strongly favor narrow CI; lower values (e.g. 0.2) allow more tolerance. Default 0.5 provides a balanced trade-off.

threshold_ci_alpha.label: CI alpha
threshold_ci_alpha.desc: Significance level for the bootstrap threshold confidence interval. Alpha=0.05 gives a 95% CI; alpha=0.10 gives a 90% CI (narrower, fewer rejections but less conservative). Smaller alpha = wider CI = more samples rejected in the uncertainty zone.

threshold_ci_frac_bootstrap.label: Bootstrap fraction
threshold_ci_frac_bootstrap.desc: Fraction of samples drawn per bootstrap replicate. 1.0 = classical Efron bootstrap (n samples drawn with replacement). Values < 1.0 use the Politis & Romano subsampling method (drawn without replacement), which can provide better coverage for dependent or heavy-tailed data. Try 0.632 for a common alternative.

user_feature_penalties_weight.label: User penalty weight
user_feature_penalties_weight.desc: Weight applied to user-defined feature penalties from feature_annotations file.

n_model_to_display.label: Models to display
n_model_to_display.desc: Number of models shown in the last generation. 0 = show all models.

display_colorful.label: Colorful output
display_colorful.desc: Enable ANSI color codes in the console output for easier reading.

population_size.label: Population size
population_size.desc: Target number of models per generation. Actual count may be lower due to clone removal.

max_epochs.label: Max epochs
max_epochs.desc: Maximum number of generations before the algorithm stops.

min_epochs.label: Min epochs
min_epochs.desc: Minimum number of generations before early stopping is allowed.

max_age_best_model.label: Max age best model
max_age_best_model.desc: Early stop (after min_epochs) if the best model reaches this age without improvement.

k_min.label: k min
k_min.desc: Minimum number of variables (features) in initial population models.

k_max.label: k max
k_max.desc: Maximum number of variables in initial population. 0 = no maximum.

select_elite_pct.label: Elite %
select_elite_pct.desc: Percentage of best models from previous generation retained. Lower = more elitist.

select_niche_pct.label: Niche %
select_niche_pct.desc: Percentage of best models retained per language/data type to maintain diversity.

select_random_pct.label: Random %
select_random_pct.desc: Percentage of opportunistic models retained from previous generation.

mutated_children_pct.label: Mutated children %
mutated_children_pct.desc: Percentage of children subjected to mutation.

mutated_features_pct.label: Mutated features %
mutated_features_pct.desc: Percentage of mutation per gene (potential variable). Most mutations are nonsensical.

mutation_non_null_chance_pct.label: Non-null mutation %
mutation_non_null_chance_pct.desc: Likelihood that a mutation adds a new variable rather than just removing one.

forced_diversity_pct.label: Forced diversity %
forced_diversity_pct.desc: If > 0%, population is filtered every N epochs to enforce diversity.

forced_diversity_epochs.label: Diversity epoch gap
forced_diversity_epochs.desc: Epochs between two diversity filters (when forced_diversity_pct > 0).

random_sampling_pct.label: Random sampling %
random_sampling_pct.desc: Stochastic subsampling: each generation is evaluated on a random subset of this percentage of training samples. Acts as implicit regularization by preventing models from overfitting to the full training set. Recommended: 70-90% for datasets with > 100 samples. 0 = use all samples (no subsampling).

random_sampling_epochs.label: Sampling epoch gap
random_sampling_epochs.desc: Number of consecutive epochs using the same random subsample before redrawing. 1 = fresh subsample every generation (maximum stochasticity). Higher values (e.g. 5) give more stable fitness estimates per epoch but less regularization effect.

n_epochs_before_global.label: Epochs before global
n_epochs_before_global.desc: Epochs of per-language competition before merging into a global population.

method.label: Method
method.desc: LimitedExhaustive: all k-combinations. ParallelForward: extend each model by one feature.

k_start.label: k start
k_start.desc: Number of variables in the initial population for beam search.

k_stop.label: k stop
k_stop.desc: Maximum number of variables in a single model.

best_models_criterion.label: Best models criterion
best_models_criterion.desc: If <= 1: alpha for FBM CI (smaller = larger range). If > 1: top X% of best models to keep.

max_nb_of_models.label: Max models
max_nb_of_models.desc: Limits features to keep at each epoch based on model count possibilities.

n_burn.label: Burn-in
n_burn.desc: Number of initial MCMC iterations to discard (typically the first half).

lambda.label: Lambda
lambda.desc: Bayesian prior parameter for coefficients a, b, c.

nmin.label: nmin
nmin.desc: Minimum features in a model after feature elimination. 0 = keep all features (disable SBS).

perturbation_size.label: Perturbation size
perturbation_size.desc: Number of random moves per perturbation (larger = more exploration).

initial_temperature.label: Initial temperature
initial_temperature.desc: Starting temperature. Higher = more initial exploration (accepts worse solutions more freely).

cooling_rate.label: Cooling rate
cooling_rate.desc: Temperature multiplier per iteration. Closer to 1.0 = slower cooling, more thorough search. 0.999 ≈ 7000 iterations to reach 0.001.

k_min.label: k min
k_min.desc: Minimum number of features per model.

k_max.label: k max
k_max.desc: Maximum number of features per model.

n_ants.label: Number of ants
n_ants.desc: Number of models constructed per iteration. More ants = better exploration but slower.

min_iterations.label: Min iterations
min_iterations.desc: Minimum iterations before early stopping is allowed.

max_age_best_model.label: Max age best model
max_age_best_model.desc: Early stop if best model hasn't improved for this many iterations.

k_min.label: k min
k_min.desc: Minimum number of features per model.

k_max.label: k max
k_max.desc: Maximum number of features per model.

alpha.label: Alpha (pheromone weight)
alpha.desc: Pheromone importance exponent. Higher = more exploitation (follow collective memory).

beta.label: Beta (heuristic weight)
beta.desc: Heuristic (feature significance) importance exponent. Higher = more bias toward statistically significant features.

rho.label: Evaporation rate (ρ)
rho.desc: Pheromone evaporation rate. Higher = faster forgetting, more exploration. Lower = longer memory, more exploitation.

elite_weight.label: Elite weight
elite_weight.desc: Extra pheromone deposit weight for the global-best ant. Controls how strongly the best-ever solution guides future ants.

n_estimators.label: Number of trees
n_estimators.desc: Number of decision trees in the forest. More trees = better performance but slower.

max_depth.label: Max depth
max_depth.desc: Maximum tree depth. null = unlimited (trees grow until pure leaves).

min_samples_split.label: Min samples split
min_samples_split.desc: Minimum samples required to split an internal node.

kernel.label: Kernel
kernel.desc: Kernel function. Linear is interpretable; RBF captures non-linearities.

C.label: Regularization (C)
C.desc: Inverse regularization strength. Smaller = more regularization.

penalty.label: Penalty
penalty.desc: Regularization type. L1 produces sparse models (feature selection), L2 shrinks coefficients.

C.label: Regularization (C)
C.desc: Inverse regularization strength. Smaller = more regularization.

l1_ratio.label: L1 ratio
l1_ratio.desc: Elastic Net mixing (0=L2, 1=L1). Only used with Elastic Net penalty.

max_depth.label: Max depth
max_depth.desc: Maximum tree depth. Controls model complexity.

learning_rate.label: Learning rate
learning_rate.desc: Step size shrinkage to prevent overfitting.

learning_rate.label: Learning rate
learning_rate.desc: Weight applied to each classifier at each boosting iteration.

n_neighbors.label: Number of neighbors
n_neighbors.desc: Number of nearest neighbors for classification.

outer_folds.label: Outer folds
outer_folds.desc: Number of outer cross-validation folds. The algorithm trains independently on each combination of k-1 folds, producing separate FBMs that are then merged. More folds = better variance estimate but longer runtime. 5 or 10 folds are standard choices.

inner_folds.label: Inner folds
inner_folds.desc: Number of inner folds for overfitting penalty estimation. Within each outer fold, the training set is further split into inner folds. The penalty is computed as the gap between training and held-out inner fold performance. Only active when overfit_penalty > 0.

overfit_penalty.label: Overfit penalty
overfit_penalty.desc: Inner-fold overfitting penalty. During evolution, each model is evaluated on inner folds; the gap between training and validation performance is penalized: fitness -= mean_gap × penalty. This discourages models that memorize training data. Recommended: 0.1-0.5 for moderate regularization. 0 = disabled (no inner-fold penalty).

resampling_inner_folds_epochs.label: Resample inner folds
resampling_inner_folds_epochs.desc: Reshuffle inner fold assignments every N epochs. Prevents the evolutionary algorithm from implicitly learning which samples are in which fold (a subtle form of information leakage). Recommended: 5-20 epochs when using overfit_penalty. 0 = never reshuffle (static folds).

fit_on_valid.label: Fit on validation
fit_on_valid.desc: FBM based on validation fold fit (favoring generalization). Requires external test data.

cv_best_models_ci_alpha.label: FBM CI alpha
cv_best_models_ci_alpha.desc: Alpha for Family of Best Models CI on best validation fit. Smaller = larger range.

stratify_by.label: Stratify by
stratify_by.desc: Stratify folds by classes AND this annotation column (from sample annotations file).

compute_importance.label: Compute importance
compute_importance.desc: Compute feature importance via Mean Decrease Accuracy (MDA).

n_permutations_mda.label: MDA permutations
n_permutations_mda.desc: Number of permutations per feature for MDA importance calculation.

scaled_importance.label: Scaled importance
scaled_importance.desc: Scale importance values by feature prevalence within folds.

importance_aggregation.label: Aggregation
importance_aggregation.desc: Method to aggregate importance scores across folds.

vote.label: Enable voting
vote.desc: Activate voting ensemble where multiple models vote on sample classification.

fbm_ci_alpha.label: FBM CI alpha
fbm_ci_alpha.desc: Alpha for Family of Best Models confidence interval. Smaller = larger best_model range.

fbm_ci_method.label: FBM CI method
fbm_ci_method.desc: Binomial CI method for Family of Best Models (FBM) selection. Wilson (recommended) provides near-nominal coverage for all sample sizes. Clopper-Pearson is conservative (widest CI, more models). Wald is simplest but has poor coverage near p=0 or p=1.

prune_before_voting.label: Prune before voting
prune_before_voting.desc: Prune models based on feature importances (remove models with MDA < 0).

min_experts.label: Min experts
min_experts.desc: Minimum number of jury experts. 0 = no minimum (use all that pass filters). Warns if fewer experts remain.

max_experts.label: Max experts
max_experts.desc: Maximum number of jury experts. 0 = no limit. Top models by fitness are kept when the limit is reached.

min_perf.label: Min performance
min_perf.desc: Required sensitivity AND specificity for a judge model. >= 0.5 avoids single-choice bias.

min_diversity.label: Min diversity
min_diversity.desc: Required diversity (feature difference count) between judge models.

method.label: Voting method
method.desc: Majority: class 1 if votes > threshold. Consensus: no classification if threshold not reached.

method_threshold.label: Voting threshold
method_threshold.desc: Typically 0.5 for Majority, 1 for Consensus. If 0, optimize via Youden maximum.

threshold_windows_pct.label: Threshold window %
threshold_windows_pct.desc: Samples with votes within threshold +/- this percentage are not classified.

complete_display.label: Complete display
complete_display.desc: Display full voting results including all individual judge contributions.

fallback_to_cpu.label: Fallback to CPU
fallback_to_cpu.desc: Execute on CPU (integrated graphics) if no discrete GPU available. Recommended.

memory_policy.label: Memory policy
memory_policy.desc: Strict: panic on limit exceeded. Adaptive: adjust if unavailable. Performance: use all GPU memory.

max_total_memory_mb.label: Max GPU memory
max_total_memory_mb.desc: Maximum total GPU memory in MB for all buffers.

max_buffer_size_mb.label: Max buffer size
max_buffer_size_mb.desc: Maximum GPU memory in MB for a single buffer.

enabled.label: Enable clinical integration
enabled.desc: Combine gpredomics omics scores with clinical variables (age, BMI, lab values, etc.) to improve predictions. Requires a clinical metadata file uploaded in the Data tab.

method.label: Integration method
method.desc: How to combine omics and clinical data.

interactions.label: Interaction terms
interactions.desc: Add interaction terms (omics_score × each clinical variable). Captures effect modification, e.g., omics score is more predictive in younger patients.

columns.label: Clinical columns
columns.desc: Comma-separated column names to use from the clinical file. Leave empty to use all numeric columns.

data.label: Attach data
data.hint: Upload a training matrix (X) and its labels (y), or pick a dataset from your library.

parameters.label: Review the parameters
parameters.hint: Pick a preset or adjust the essentials; the defaults are ready to run.

launch.label: Launch an analysis
launch.hint: Use the Launch button at the bottom of the Parameters tab.

results.label: Look at the results
results.hint: Open the Results tab once the job has completed.

step1.title: Your data
step1.help: Two text files are needed: the measurements (one row per feature, one column per sample) and the group of each sample.
step1.xHint: Features in rows, samples in columns (.tsv or .csv)
step1.yHint: One line per sample: sample name, then its group (0 or 1)
step1.formatTitle: What should the files look like?
step1.formatText: Tab- or comma-separated text. The first file has one row per feature; the second gives the group of each sample. Sample names must match.

step2.title: Run the analysis
step2.help: Predomics looks for a small set of features that tells the two groups apart. Choose how long it may search.
step2.readOnly: You can view this project but not run analyses in it.

quick.name: Quick
quick.desc: A first look. Good to check that the data load correctly.

thorough.name: Thorough
thorough.desc: A larger search checked by cross-validation. For results you will report.

step3.title: Result
step3.running: The analysis is running. You can leave this page; it carries on.
step3.empty: The result will appear here once an analysis has run.

result.noTest: This score is measured on the samples used to build the model, so it is optimistic. Use the Thorough setting, or add a test set in Expert mode, for an honest estimate.
result.overfit: The model does much better on the training samples ({train}) than on the test samples ({test}): it is likely over-fitted.
result.signatureHelp: The model adds up the features on one side and subtracts those on the other. These lists are the features it uses.
result.openExpert: See every detail in Expert mode

excellent.title: Excellent separation
excellent.text: The groups are told apart almost perfectly. Check that this holds on independent samples before drawing conclusions.

good.title: Good separation
good.text: The signature separates the groups well.

fair.title: Moderate separation
fair.text: There is a real but partial difference between the groups.

weak.title: Weak separation
weak.text: The signature does only slightly better than chance.

chance.title: No clear separation
chance.text: The model does not tell the groups apart better than chance with these data.
